24 Each of the principal radiations of the electromagnetic spectrum has a range of wavelengths.
Which wavelength is correctly linked to its radiation?

X-ray

hints: Notice the four wavelengths span $10^{-14} \text{ m}$ to $10^{-5} \text{ m}$ - recall the order of decreasing wavelength from microwaves down to gamma rays.

Recall typical boundaries: gamma rays below $10^{-11} \text{ m}$, X-rays $10^{-11} \text{ m}$ to $10^{-8} \text{ m}$, ultraviolet $10^{-9} \text{ m}$ to $10^{-7} \text{ m}$, infrared around $10^{-6} \text{ m}$ to $10^{-3} \text{ m}$.
Compare each given power of ten in $\text{m}$ with those ranges to see which pairing falls inside its band and which are one or more bands too high or too low.
walkthrough: List the spectrum in order of increasing wavelength: gamma rays, X-rays, ultraviolet, visible, infrared, microwaves.

Recall approximate wavelengths in $\text{m}$: gamma rays $<10^{-11}$, X-rays $10^{-11}$ to $10^{-8}$, ultraviolet $10^{-9}$ to $4 \times 10^{-7}$, infrared $10^{-6}$ to $10^{-3}$, microwaves $10^{-3}$ to $10^{-1}$.
Check $10^{-9} \text{ m}$ against gamma rays: it is about 100 to 10000 times too long and fits X-rays, so that pairing fails.
Check $10^{-5} \text{ m}$ against microwaves: it is about 100 times too short and fits infrared, so that pairing fails.
Check $10^{-14} \text{ m}$ against X-rays: it is about 1000 times too short and fits gamma rays, so that pairing fails.
Check $10^{-8} \text{ m}$ against ultraviolet: it lies clearly between X-rays and visible light inside the ultraviolet band, so this pairing holds. This is option C

A.explanation: A wavelength of $10^{-9} \text{ m}$ is in the X-ray region, not gamma rays which have much shorter wavelengths below about $10^{-11} \text{ m}$.

B.explanation: A wavelength of $10^{-5} \text{ m}$ is in the infrared region, not microwaves which have much longer wavelengths around $10^{-3} \text{ m}$ to $10^{-1} \text{ m}$.

C.explanation: A wavelength of $10^{-8} \text{ m}$ lies between X-rays and visible light, which is the ultraviolet range of about $10^{-9} \text{ m}$ to $4 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$.

D.explanation: A wavelength of $10^{-14} \text{ m}$ is in the gamma-ray region, not X-rays which have longer wavelengths around $10^{-11} \text{ m}$ to $10^{-8} \text{ m}$.
